## Content Feed Curator

**Daily 00:00** Europe/Madrid (midnight). This workflow **tops up a backlog**; LinkedIn Post Sharing drains exactly one row of it per run and keeps its own schedule of 3 posts a week (Mon 16:00, Wed/Fri 10:30). Filling faster never publishes more: the publish rate is set there, not here.

It was Sun/Tue/Thu 06:00, which made it a batch job that had to fill a whole week in three runs. Daily is a top-up and it is nearly free once the backlog is deep - `pick_finalists` sets the judge budget from the room each category actually has, so a full category spends zero calls. The 24-call runs happen while **filling**, roughly the first fortnight. Daily also gets a `NEWS_REACTION` article into the queue within a day of publication instead of up to three.

**Three categories: Data, AI, DevOps.** Tech and News are in `exclude_categories`, so Miniflux is never even asked for them. Tech used to carry weight 0.65 instead, which was not enough - unfilled quota redistributes by weight, so Tech took 14 of 60 pool slots against a quota of 9 and the judge blocked most of them. Each remaining category now gets ~20 of the 60 slots instead of ~13.

**Hacker News is a source, not a category.** Its candidates are routed into the three by title against `category_keywords`; one matching nothing is dropped and counted as `hn unrouted`. The old `HN` category drew a quota of 12 and filled 2, because HN links are correctly merged into the publisher's copy by `filter_candidates` before ranking - which is where HN's value is, since only HN knows the vote count.

**Two sources, one LLM stage:**
Miniflux (per category, News and Tech never fetched) + Hacker News front page
-> free filters and same-story merge -> free pre-rank into a **quota-allocated** pool
-> HN engagement lookup -> cut to `judge_n`
-> **one judge call per finalist, on the full article**
-> admit to the backlog, up to the room it has.

**The queue is durable.** Sharing publishes exactly one row per run (`select_article_to_post` ends in `slice(0,1)`), so the old design spent 16 judge calls to build a five-item slate, published one and expired the other four - then re-fetched and re-judged them next run. Nothing is thrown away now until it goes stale (TTL from the judge's `hook`) or over cap. That is why there is no `top_n` and no per-slate diversity caps: **variety is decided on the way out**, by topic rotation in `select_article_to_post`, which guarantees it across a week instead of fighting for it inside one run.

One backlog per category, `max_per_category` deep, keyed on `TOPIC`. A link lives in exactly one of them - `admit_to_backlog` rejects any URL already anywhere in the sheet, whatever its STATUS or category.

**`write_to_sheet` is now `true`.** Every run before this was a dry run, which is why the digest said `Backlog 0 -> 4` three runs running: nothing was ever appended, so the backlog could not accumulate and the sheet dedupe had nothing to match - the same articles were re-judged at full cost every run. `mark_read` is still `false` on purpose; flip it after one real run appends cleanly, since it marks ~800 Miniflux entries read and runs after the append.

Nothing placed by hand is ever at risk: `build_expire_rows` filters on `ORIGIN === 'AUTO'` as an allow-list, so only rows the curator wrote itself can be deleted.

**Env vars:** `MINIFLUX_URL`, `MINIFLUX_API_USER`, `MINIFLUX_API_PASSWORD`. Hacker News needs no credentials.

**Reddit was removed.** `top.json` 403s unauthenticated clients; `top.rss` worked for one run then 429'd sub after sub even at 7s spacing with the order rotated by day. Best run: 5 candidates of 839, none admitted. Bringing it back needs a registered OAuth app. `reddit.com` stays in `aggregator_hosts` and `reddit.com/r/` in `domain_blocklist` - Miniflux still carries the r/programming feed, whose entry URLs are comment threads.

**TTLs were raised** to `NEWS_REACTION 10 / HARD_NUMBER 45 / default 60`. `NEWS_REACTION` was 4 against a `lookback_days` of 5, so a news item at the edge of the intake window was judged, admitted and expired without ever reaching a publish slot - and one at 2.65 days old (postability 8, VERY_HIGH) got exactly one shot at the Monday slot. Every TTL must clear `lookback_days` + the longest publish gap (Fri -> Mon = 3), so the floor is 8; the digest raises a siren if any drops under it. `HARD_NUMBER` also had the shortest non-news TTL, which was backwards - a measured number does not go stale.

**The backlog is a quality buffer, not a queue.** Rotation touches ~3 topics a week, so one category publishes ~0.6 times a week and its 10th row would need a 100+ day TTL to reach a slot. Most rows expire unpublished by design - each slot picks the best row in a deep, fresh pool. The cost is judge calls, and it is self-limiting: `pick_finalists` skips categories already at `max_per_category`, so the 24-call runs happen while FILLING and steady state is cheap.

nodes.name: schedule_trigger
nodes.notes:
Sun/Tue/Thu 06:00 Europe/Madrid - the day BEFORE each publish slot, so every slot is preceded by a fresh top-up and the two jobs never touch content_queue on the same day. LinkedIn Post Sharing stays at 3 posts a week (Mon 16:00, Wed/Fri 10:30); this job only fills the backlog, it never decides how much gets published.
lookback_days must cover the longest gap between runs plus slack for a failed one: Thu -> Sun is 3 days, and Thu -> Tue is 5 if the Sunday run fails, which is why it is 5.

nodes.name: fetch_candidates
nodes.notes: Miniflux per non-excluded category, plus the Hacker News front page above a points floor. Each source in its own try/catch. Reddit was removed - 403/429 without an OAuth app.

nodes.name: read_legacy_sheet

### Everything free happens before the judge

`fetch_candidates` asks both sources - each in its own try/catch, so a dead source is a digest warning, not a failed run.

`filter_candidates` drops what the blocklists and the sheet already answer for, and **merges** same-story duplicates instead of discarding them: only Hacker News knows the vote count, so the surviving copy inherits it.

`rank_candidates` ranks on topic keyword affinity, a hard number in the headline, recency and votes - no network, no tokens - then **allocates** the pool by `category_weights` rather than filling it first-come. A flat per-category ceiling gave Tech 20 of 60 slots while Hacker News contributed 40 candidates and got 1: a bare link has no excerpt to match keywords against, so it loses to any full article. Each category now competes only against itself. Watch `quota -> filled` in the digest.

`pick_finalists` sets the judge budget from the room the backlog actually has, **per category**, at four calls per free slot. `judge_n` is a ceiling, not a target: a full backlog spends zero, and a category already at `max_per_category` is skipped rather than judged and rejected downstream. The digest names any category that stopped listening.

Only two numbers cost anything: `max_candidates` bounds the HN lookups, `judge_n` bounds the LLM calls.

nodes.name: if_thin_content
nodes.notes: Miniflux has no crawler:true on any feed, so excerpt-only feeds are common. Only those pay for puppeteer.

nodes.name: download_full_content
nodes.notes: Reuses the existing Download Content workflow (Freedium/puppeteer/anti-captcha). Failure is tolerated - the judge falls back to the excerpt.

nodes.name: ai_model
nodes.notes: Judge stage: the quality gate, so it keeps the primary model.

nodes.name: if_write_to_sheet
nodes.notes: False keeps the run a dry run: digest only, sheet untouched.

nodes.name: expire_auto_queue
nodes.notes: ORIGIN=AUTO + STATUS=QUEUE only, and only rows past their hook TTL or over the backlog cap. Manual rows and anything past QUEUE are never touched. Most runs expire nothing.

nodes.name: append_content_queue
nodes.notes: Appends whatever cleared the judge and had backlog room - typically 0-6 rows, not a fixed slate.

nodes.name: mark_entries_read
nodes.notes: Marks every fetched Miniflux entry read so it is never scored twice - this is what stops the same candidates being re-judged every run. Hacker News candidates have no entry_id. Skipped while curator_config.mark_read is false.

### The switch is done

**LinkedIn Post Sharing now reads `content_queue`.** All six of its Google Sheets nodes were repointed, and `update_status_error` writes `ERROR` + `EXECUTION_ID` back to the row so a failed post leaves a trace.

`articles_2_linkedin` is frozen history. Nothing was migrated out of it - the old queue is deliberately forgotten. `read_legacy_sheet` still reads it, purely so the curator never re-curates something already published from it.

`select_article_to_post` has `AVOID_LAST = 1`, down from 2. With three categories, 2 would leave exactly one category eligible and publish order would override `PRIORITY` outright. At 1 the same topic still can never go out twice in a row, and priority chooses between the other two.

Left to do: flip `mark_read` to `true` once a real run has appended cleanly.

### Watch on the next runs

- `Backlog N -> M` and its per-category depth. A category at 0 cannot be published from, and rotation will skip past it rather than fix it.
- `quota -> filled`. **This is the only signal that says whether adding RSS feeds would help.** More feeds do not raise output - `max_candidates` and `judge_n` bind, not supply, and 648 of 834 raw candidates were already discarded by the pool cap. They raise the QUALITY of the 60, which raises the judge yield. So feed whichever category comes in *under* quota: Data filled 12 of 13 while Tech absorbed 5 redistributed slots it had not earned. `HN` at 2 of 12 is not that signal - its duplicates are correctly merged into the publisher's copy upstream.
- `cleared/judged` per category. This is the input to the `category_weights` decision: `News` is zeroed, and `Tech` at 0.65 has never had data behind it. If Tech runs at 1/9 while Data runs at 4/4 over three runs, zero Tech too and those pool slots go to categories that convert.
- `judge verdict(s) came back unusable` - one article each now, but a run of them means the model, not the batch size.
- Whether HN rows clear `min_postability`. They are bare links, so each one costs a Download Content fetch.

### The blank-row bug

`append_content_queue` used to hang straight off `if_write_to_sheet`, which is four nodes past `admit_to_backlog` - and `notify_digest` replaces the stream with Slack's API response. Every `={{ $json.URL }}` mapping resolved to `undefined`, so it appended ONE BLANK ROW per run and reported success, because an append of undefined values is not an error. `build_queue_rows` re-emits the admitted rows one item each, immediately before the append.

`if_has_admissions` sits in front of it so a run that admits nothing still reaches `if_mark_read`. In steady state most runs admit zero, and hanging mark-read off the append would mean the Miniflux window never prunes again. Ordering is deliberate: mark-read stays downstream of the append, so entries are never marked read before the write lands.
